doc.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: The Frank Zappa date and Ian Underwood
summary: He recounts a late-night session for Zappa's Lumpy Gravy, Zappa's praise, and Ian Underwood's synthesizer mastery.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: What was let’s say the most obvious rock & roll date that you may have participated in, or was there any?
I did one date with Frank Zappa.
No kidding?
Yeah. “Lumpy Gravy” or something.
You were on “Lumpy Gravy?” Get out.

I’m trying to think of these names that I’ve worked with, it’s a lot of years. And you know what he said to me when I was on the date? It was a late date, it didn’t start until like one o’clock or eleven thirty at night. And I remember leaving the house and thinking oh boy, it’s going to be one of those long dates at Capitol over here. So he says, he was very complimentary, he says, “Pete I remember when I was going to high school up in Lancaster, and you were playing with Shorty Rodgers, and you guys came by and you just killed me, I loved it.”
Cool.
Yeah, that was Frank Zappa.
He had quite band, Ian Underwood and—
Ian, yeah.
And some of those guys.
Yeah. I used to work with Ian a lot in the studios.
Yeah he became quite a studio ace didn’t he?

Oh on every date he’d be there, because he was one of the first guys that got into synths. I mean he was patching all the time. I mean back in those days, he was patching. Chords galore. And I’m looking at him like whoa. I don’t think I could ever get into that. But he was a master at it.
Did you enjoy that date?
Yeah it was interesting. It’s sort of like I don’t know quite what to expect. It came off. It was a challenge though, I remember it was a little bit different.
Was it a live session or were you doing overdubs?
It was a live session. I don’t think I’m on all the tracks, but I’m on some of them.
I’ll have to get that album out and—
Yeah, I don’t even have it myself, but I know I’m on it.
